findings.title: The inherited production-compiler source commitment is still incomplete
findings.consequence: Fresh bodies reproduce today, but the sealed productionSourceClosure does not commit the complete code graph that produces them; the known v2 provenance defect remains.
findings.requiredCorrection: Commit the exact sorted 191-file local compiler graph, all literal dynamic imports and runtime data inputs with exact bytes/SHA-256, then rebuild and audit a new immutable version.

findings.title: The response parser accepts non-terminal, schema-invalid candidate evidence and fractional token usage
findings.consequence: The runner can count a truncated or structurally invalid response as a successful settled assignment, so strict response and usage evidence is not established.
findings.requiredCorrection: Require an allowed terminal finish reason, validate the complete question against the committed response schema, and require safe-integer token counters before success.

passes: All 15 v2 package files match the prior independent-review baseline exactly.

Test support is network-incapable and outside the live closure.

The sole model-dispatch call site is production-runner.ts; current protocol authorization flags are false and the operator CLI is unconditionally dormant.

Both stored wire bodies freshly reproduce from the current production compiler and bind Standard Gemini 3.5 Flash then Premium Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, google-vertex/global only, reasoning off, one completion/candidate/fetch each.
Failure, timeout, and unknown-after-send stop the serial loop without replay.
The public result key set equals the protocol allowlist and excludes raw/private evidence.
The global ledger remains 0 used / 0 reserved of 1000; source implements an exclusive-lock atomic +2 global reservation and a private +2 reservation.

The price schema requires freshness, canonical slugs, exact endpoint/cardinality, all returned active endpoints and overrides, charge dimensions, and a self content hash; the collector was not executed.
